% Converted, ltx-talk, C-GLYPH-MISSING workaround applied: the character comes from a font
% that has it. pifont's \ding{51} renders, extracts as a correct U+2713, logs no Missing
% character, and passes verapdf -f ua2 -- verified on this file.
%
% Things that do NOT work: \checkmark from amssymb OR from wasysym, and a literal ✓ typed
% into the source, all three identically. The default text font NewCMSans10-Regular has no
% U+2713, so LuaTeX drops the character, and the package that names it is irrelevant.
%
% Alternative, if you want the literal character to stay in the source:
%   \usepackage{newunicodechar}\usepackage{pifont}
%   \newunicodechar{✓}{\ding{51}}
% Also verified clean. Not used here because the fixture should test the smaller change.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}
\usepackage{pifont}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
\frametitle{Coverage}
Marked A \ding{51} B done.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
